faqs.question: How do I get to Kurinbi Island?
faqs.answer: Public ferry service operates weekly from Male (approximately 14 hours journey time). Private speedboat transfers can be arranged through guesthouses (approximately 7 hours from Male).

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Kurinbi Island?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit Kurinbi Island is during the northeast monsoon season (December to April), which brings dry, sunny weather with lower humidity and calmer seas. Water temperature remains warm (26-29°C/79-84°F) throughout the year.

faqs.question: What makes Kurinbi different from other local islands in the Maldives?
faqs.answer: Kurinbi stands out for its northern location (with distinct marine life), authentic preservation of traditional northern Maldivian life, and peaceful atmosphere. Unlike more developed islands, Kurinbi maintains its authentic character with a community still primarily engaged in traditional fishing and crafts.

faqs.question: Are there any dress code requirements on Kurinbi Island?
faqs.answer: As Kurinbi is a local inhabited island with a Muslim population, visitors are expected to dress modestly in public areas (shoulders and knees covered). Swimwear is only permitted at the designated "bikini beach." When visiting the mosque or religious sites, women should cover their heads. These requirements don't apply during water activities or at resort day visits.

faqs.question: What marine life can I expect to see while snorkeling around Kurinbi?
faqs.answer: Kurinbi's waters offer unique northern marine biodiversity, including healthy coral formations with both hard and soft corals. Common sightings include reef fish species that may differ from central/southern atolls, sea turtles, various ray species, and seasonal visitors. The house reef provides easy access to this underwater world directly from shore.
